title: Conormal representatives of sheaf cotangent Ext classes after changing generators
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and let $G$ be a $B$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}$ and, for a sheaf of sets $E$ over $B$, the sheaf polynomial presentation $P_E\to B$, its kernel $J_E$, the complex $K_E=[J_E/J_E^2\to\Omega_{P_E/A}\otimes_{P_E}B]$ and its canonical comparison $\lambda_E$ from [lem-sfb-sheaf-polynomial-cotangent-comparison]. Use derived Ext [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the boundary $\partial_E$ of [lem-sfb-two-term-derived-hom-boundary]. For every $\xi\in\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A},G)$, there exist a sheaf of sets $E$, a map $E\to B$ inducing a surjection of sheaves $A[E]\to B$, and a $B$-linear sheaf map $\delta:J_E/J_E^2\to G$ such that
$$\xi=\partial_E(\delta)\circ\lambda_E^{-1}\quad\text{in }\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))}(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A},G[1]).$$

proof.text: Start with $E=B$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. Evaluation is sectionwise surjective, since a section $b$ is the image of the variable $[b]$. Use the comparison node to form $M=J_E/J_E^2$, $F=\Omega_{P_E/A}\otimes B$, $K=K_E$ and $\lambda=\lambda_E$. Set $x=\xi\lambda\in\operatorname{Hom}_D(K,G[1])$. The new polynomial-differentials lemma identifies $F$ naturally with $B^{(E)}$; let $i:E\to|F|$ send $e$ to $\mathrm d[e]\otimes1$.

Let $j:F[0]\to K$ be the inclusion and $q:K\to M[1]$ the quotient. The cone of the chain map $d:M[0]\to F[0]$ has terms $M,F$ in degrees $-1,0$ with differential $d$, hence is $K$ by the cone formula in the derived-category definition. Its distinguished cone triangle, rotated once, has first two maps $j$ and $\epsilon q$, with $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$ depending only on the fixed cone convention. Exactness of Hom out of a distinguished triangle says that any $y:K\to G[1]$ with $yj=0$ is $b\epsilon q$ for some $b:M[1]\to G[1]$. Shifting identifies $b$ with a derived map $M[0]\to G[0]$; the degree-zero isomorphism in the two-term boundary node, applied to $[0\to M]$, identifies this with an actual module map. Absorbing $\epsilon$ in that map gives $y=\partial_E(\delta)$. Thus it suffices to kill the obstruction $\eta=xj\in\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(F,G)$.

The category of $B$-module sheaves is abelian by the module-category node. The degree-one Yoneda/derived comparison represents $\eta$ by a short exact sequence $0\to G\to H\xrightarrow{p}F\to0$. Define the sheaf $E'=E\times_{|F|}|H|$ using $i$ and $p$, with projection $v:E'\to E$ and second projection $a:E'\to|H|$. These are sectionwise fibre products of sheaves, so they are sheaves, and $pa=iv$. The underlying abelian map of $p$ is epic: its cokernel is the same sheafified sectionwise quotient as the cokernel of $p$ in modules, by the module-category node. The general-site abelian epimorphism lemma therefore gives local lifts in $H$ of every $i(e)$, hence local lifts in $E'$ of every $e\in E(U)$. Put $\alpha'=\alpha v$. Since $E=B$, every local section $b$ of $B$ locally lifts to $e'\in E'$ with $\alpha'(e')=b$. Evaluation $A[E']\to B$ is consequently surjective as a sheaf map.

Form $K'=K_{E'}$, $F'=\Omega_{P_{E'}/A}\otimes B$ and $t=K(v):K'\to K$. Let $f=F(v):F'\to F$. By natural freeness and the free-module universal property, $a:E'\to|H|$ extends to a $B$-linear map $s:F'\to H$. On a generator $e'=(e,h)$ one has $p s(\mathrm d[e']\otimes1)=p(h)=i(e)=f(\mathrm d[e']\otimes1)$; uniqueness in the same universal property gives $ps=f$. The pullback extension $0\to G\to H\times_F F'\to F'\to0$ is split by $z\mapsto(s(z),z)$. Naturality of the Yoneda/derived comparison and its split-zero clause give $\eta f=0$ in $\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(F',G)$.

Write $j':F'[0]\to K'$ for the inclusion. The chain map $t$ has degree-zero component $f$, so $tj'=jf$. Hence $(xt)j'=xjf=\eta f=0$. Apply the exactness argument of step 2 to $K'$ to obtain a module map $\delta:J_{E'}/J_{E'}^2\to G$ with $xt=\partial_{E'}(\delta)$. The comparison node gives $\lambda_{E}t=\lambda_{E'}$, and therefore $\xi\lambda_{E'}=\xi\lambda_Et=xt=\partial_{E'}(\delta)$. Compose on the right with $\lambda_{E'}^{-1}$ and rename $E'$ as $E$. This is the required equality with a surjective polynomial presentation.

lean.statement: theorem sheaf_cotangent_ext_representative {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : Precoverage C) (_hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings) (A B : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck CommRingCat.{u}) (f : A ⟶ B) (D : Comparison f) (G : ringedSiteModules.{u} (siteModuleRings B)) (ξ : (localization B).obj (D.models (canonical f)).complex ⟶ ((localization B).obj ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor _ 0).obj G))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) : ∃ (P : Presentation f) (δ : (D.models P).complex.X (-1) ⟶ G), ξ = (D.lambda P).inv ≫ @DerivedCategory.twoTermSupportedBoundary _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _) (D.models P).complex (D.models P).supported G δ
lean.note: Uses the dependency Comparison data explicitly, for every such normalized model, rather than making an uncharacterized choice from its existence theorem. Presentation bundles exactly E, its map to B, and sheaf-surjectivity of polynomial evaluation. The conormal module is the comparison model degree -1 term, whose local quotient and kernel are specified by the dependency. Derived Ext is written as derived Hom into G[1] with HasDerivedCategory.standard. The item module contains the canonical supported-complex boundary helpers; the recorded two-term boundary dependency and its module remain unchanged.
